text.p: Jordan has cracked down on a group of "professional" beggars who were so successful they used mobile phones to chat to each other, the official Petra news agency said on Wednesday.
It said the Committee to Combat Begging and Vagrancy had swooped on 221 beggars around the country.

"Most of those detained took up begging as a career and weren't in need of assistance," Petra quoted committee sources as saying. "Some beggars were arrested using mobile phones to talk to each other."
The committee urged Jordanians not to give money to beggars, saying the poor were cared for by the Ministry of Social Development.
Unskilled public sector workers can earn as little as 100 dinars ($140) a month in Jordan and unemployment is high in the poorer south of the country.
